name: Security depth
description: What the built-in security lens's pattern counts cannot see: unauthenticated writes, missing owner or tenant scoping, injection reached from request input, loose CORS, secrets in client config, vulnerable dependencies and weak sessions. Judged by reading the context's code.

fields.label: Unauthenticated writes
fields.description: Mutating handlers reachable with no authentication, unsigned webhooks included.

fields.label: Authorization gaps
fields.description: Authenticated handlers that read or change a record by a request id without scoping it to the caller's owner, tenant or role (IDOR).

fields.label: Reachable injection sinks
fields.description: Request input reaching string-built SQL or NoSQL, a shell, a file path or a server-side fetch of a user URL (SSRF).

fields.label: Loose CORS
fields.description: CORS that reflects any Origin, or allows any origin on an authenticated or credentialed API.

fields.label: Secrets in client
fields.description: Secrets carried by public env prefixes or shipped client config. Publishable keys are not secrets.

fields.label: High dependency advisories
fields.description: Resolved dependency versions with a high or critical advisory, counted only from an audit tool's output; otherwise left unread and noted unverified.

fields.label: Session weaknesses
fields.description: Session cookies without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite, tokens in localStorage, tokens with no expiry or unverified signature, no invalidation on logout.

rules.reason: {authzGaps} handlers do not scope records to the caller
{injectionSinks} injection sinks reachable from request input
{depVulnsHigh} dependencies with high or critical advisories

scan.instructions: Judge authentication, authorization and input handling on every route the context exposes. The built-in security lens already counts regex hits (secretHits, unsafeSinks); this lens counts only what you can show is reachable. Evidence rules - a finding that breaks one is not counted: (1) each finding names file:line, the reachable entry point (route, server action, GraphQL mutation, webhook, job) and one sentence on why an attacker reaches it; no file:line, no count. (2) Count only shipped code: never tests, fixtures, seeds, admin scripts no route calls, dead code. (3) Before counting, try to refute it: trace the middleware, base controller, policy or row-level rule in front of the handler. Protection counts only if you point to the file:line where it is configured - Next middleware matcher or a session check in the handler; Express router-level auth; ASP.NET [Authorize] or a fallback policy ([AllowAnonymous] overrides it); Django login_required or DRF DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES; FastAPI Depends on an auth dependency; Spring SecurityFilterChain matchers. (4) One root cause is one finding listing every entry it reaches. (5) Never guess versions or CVEs: write 'unverified' and name the tool that would confirm. (6) Per finding suggest a tier 0-3 and a risk_class (secret|authz|money|data|llm|perf|reliability|ux|debt) per lens-scan references/triage.md. (7) A context with no handlers, config or dependencies of its own is not applicable, with a one-line reason; 0 means judged and clean. Doubtful cases go under 'unconfirmed' and never raise a count. Fields: unauthRoutes - POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, server actions, mutations and webhooks with no authn; a webhook is protected only by a verified signature (tier 0, authz). authzGaps - a record loaded or changed by a request id with no owner, tenant or role filter (findUnique({id}) with no userId or orgId, Find(id) then save, get_object_or_404 without owner, no RLS policy); show the query (tier 0, authz). injectionSinks - request input into string-built SQL, raw NoSQL operators from the body ($where, $ne), exec/spawn/Process.Start/subprocess with shell, path joins for file access, or a server fetch of a user URL; parameterized queries and ORM builders are safe (tier 0, data). corsLoose - reflected Origin or * with credentials or on an authenticated API (tier 1, authz). secretsInClient - a secret under NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, EXPO_PUBLIC_ or in shipped config; publishable keys (Stripe pk_, a Supabase anon key with RLS you can show) are not secrets; name, never print (tier 0, secret). depVulnsHigh - count only from an audit's output (npm audit, dotnet list package --vulnerable, pip-audit, mvn dependency-check) that you ran or found; without one leave the field unread and write 'unverified' (tier 1, data). sessionWeakness - cookie flags missing, tokens in localStorage, JWT with no exp, alg none or unverified, no server-side logout (tier 1, authz).
